result.title: Delivered, Not Used: Evaluating Agent Memory at Its Point of Use
result.summary: Task success, retrieval quality, and cost do not show whether an LLM agent used a delivered memory or what followed from that use. We introduce MemUse, which evaluates memory at its point of use in recorded trajectories: each memory delivery is compared with what the agent could already see and followed through the agent's later actions and their consequences. An agentic judge rates each delivered entry's relevance, accuracy, novelty, influence, and observed effect; programmatic checks enforce complete reading of cited evidence, and fixed rules aggregate the ratings into verdicts linked to memory histories and delivery cost. On 8,000 SWE-bench Verified episodes from three memory systems, resolve rates stay within 0.4 percentage points of a no-memory baseline, yet MemUse shows that most delivered entries were irrelevant, most relevant entries went unused, and in two systems most deliveries restated content the agent could still see. It also surfaces effects that outcomes hide: 23.2\% of episodes with beneficial memory use still failed, and 5 of 16 with harmful use still succeeded.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 MemUse，在已录制的 agent 轨迹上按「使用点」评估记忆：用 agentic judge 对每条交付记忆打相关性、准确性、新颖性、影响力和实际效果，配合程序化检查与固定规则聚合成结论，并在 8,000 条 SWE-bench Verified 轨迹上发现多数交付记忆无关或未被使用，且结果指标与无记忆基线几乎持平。
AI.relevance_reason: 「交付≠使用」的判定思路与 LVR 中「答案是否真正使用视觉或 latent 内容、如何做贡献分配」高度同构，其新颖性/影响力/后果分离评价及把因果作用与任务成功解耦的做法，可供核查能否迁移到视觉证据筛选与 latent 状态利用的评估。
